business_rules.name: Route batch control requests by function code
business_rules.description: Route batch control requests by function code. The batch control subprogram selects its processing path from the caller's function code: 'INIT' sets process mode I and initialises the batch, 'CHEK' sets mode C and checks prerequisites, 'UPDT' sets mode U and updates status, and 'TERM' sets mode F and terminates the batch. Any other function code is rejected with the error text 'Invalid function code' and return code 8. Implemented in program BCHCTL00, paragraph 0000-MAIN.

condition.text: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN FUNC-INIT / FUNC-CHEK / FUNC-UPDT / FUNC-TERM / OTHER

business_rules.description: Require batch prerequisites to be satisfied. When the prerequisites-satisfied indicator (WS-PREREQ-MET = 'Y') is on, the system returns code 0 to the caller. Otherwise, the system returns warning code 4. The indicator is set only in paragraph 2200-CHECK-DEPENDENCIES, which is not present in the source, so the criteria for 'satisfied' are not documented. Implemented in program BCHCTL00, paragraph 2000-CHECK-PREREQUISITES.

outcomes.when_true: LS-RETURN-CODE = 0 (success)

business_rules.name: Route checkpoint requests by entry point
business_rules.sme_review_note: The four condition names ENTRY-POINT-INIT / -TAKE / -COMMIT / -RESTART are declared nowhere in the program or its copybooks (field_id_unresolved), so the selector field and its values are unknown; every routed paragraph is an empty stub; program logic_status partial and would not compile as written.
business_rules.description: Route checkpoint requests by entry point. The checkpoint/restart subprogram tests four entry-point conditions (initialise, take checkpoint, commit checkpoint, restart) and performs a matching paragraph; each of those paragraphs contains no executable statements, and when no condition is true nothing is performed. The field and values behind the conditions are not declared, so the business purpose cannot be confirmed from the code. Implemented in program CKPRST, unnamed first paragraph.

condition.text: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN ENTRY-POINT-INIT / ENTRY-POINT-TAKE / ENTRY-POINT-COMMIT / ENTRY-POINT-RESTART (no WHEN OTHER)

business_rules.name: Cap run error count at 100 before stopping the processing loop
business_rules.description: Cap run error count at 100 before stopping the processing loop. The main processing loop repeats until the input is exhausted or the run's error count exceeds 100; once more than 100 errors have been counted the loop stops and the program proceeds to termination. In HISTLD00 the counted errors are non-duplicate DB2 insert failures during the history load. Implemented in programs HISTLD00 (paragraph 0000-MAIN) and PORTTRAN (paragraph 0000-MAIN).

outcomes.when_true: Stop the processing loop and proceed to termination

business_rules.merge_note: Merged (M1) across programs: COND-HISTLD00-0000-L01 and COND-PORTTRAN-0000-L01 share category LIMIT_CHECK, pattern MULTI_CONDITION, subject field name WS-ERROR-COUNT, operator > and literal 100, and both combine the cap with an END-OF-FILE 88-level. The Field IDs differ (SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0044-FLD-000005 vs SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0072-FLD-000005) because each program declares its own counter; the merge is by name per the deduplication criteria. What is counted as an error differs: HISTLD00 counts non-duplicate DB2 insert failures, PORTTRAN counts every error passed to 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE (including open errors).

business_rules.name: Enforce commit and checkpoint every 1000 loaded history records
business_rules.description: Enforce commit and checkpoint every 1000 loaded history records. When the number of records loaded since the last commit reaches the commit threshold (1000, a constant), the system commits the DB2 unit of work, resets the commit counter to zero and writes a checkpoint to the batch control record. Otherwise loading continues without committing. Implemented in program HISTLD00, paragraph 2300-CHECK-COMMIT.

outcomes.when_true: EXEC SQL COMMIT WORK; MOVE 0 TO WS-COMMIT-COUNT; PERFORM 2310-UPDATE-CHECKPOINT

business_rules.name: Calculate history load counters per record
business_rules.description: Calculate history load counters per record (per-iteration rule). For each history record read the system adds 1 to records read; for each successful insert into POSHIST it adds 1 to records written; for each insert failure other than a duplicate key it adds 1 to the error count. Duplicate-key rows are counted in neither written nor errors. Implemented in program HISTLD00, paragraphs 2100-READ-HISTORY and 2200-LOAD-TO-DB2.

condition.text: ADD 1 TO WS-RECORDS-READ (line 138); ADD 1 TO WS-RECORDS-WRITTEN (line 166); ADD 1 TO WS-ERROR-COUNT (line 171)

outcomes.result: records read, records written and error count are incremented by 1 per qualifying event

business_rules.name: Derive checkpoint totals in the batch control record
business_rules.sme_review_note: Target fields BCT-RECORDS-READ and BCT-RECORDS-WRITTEN are not declared in BATCH-CONTROL-RECORD or elsewhere (field_id_unresolved); SME should confirm where the checkpoint totals are stored.
business_rules.description: Derive checkpoint totals in the batch control record (accumulated-result rule). At every commit the running totals of records read and records written are copied into the batch control record and the record is rewritten; the commit counter then restarts at zero. The two target fields are not declared in the batch control record layout. Implemented in program HISTLD00, paragraph 2310-UPDATE-CHECKPOINT.

condition.text: MOVE WS-RECORDS-READ TO BCT-RECORDS-READ; MOVE WS-RECORDS-WRITTEN TO BCT-RECORDS-WRITTEN; reset WS-COMMIT-COUNT

outcomes.result: batch control record holds the running read/written totals as of the last commit

business_rules.name: Route process sequence requests by function code
business_rules.description: Route process sequence requests by function code. The process-sequence manager selects its path from the caller's function code: 'INIT' builds the process sequence and creates READY control records, 'NEXT' finds the next process to run, 'STAT' checks status, and 'TERM' terminates the sequence. Any other code is rejected with 'Invalid function code' and return code 8. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 0000-MAIN.

condition.text: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN FUNC-INIT / FUNC-NEXT / FUNC-STAT / FUNC-TERM / OTHER

business_rules.name: Require all dependency checks to pass before starting a process
business_rules.description: Require all dependency checks to pass before starting a process. When the return code is still zero after all dependency checks, the system marks the selected process ACTIVE with its start time. Otherwise the process is not started and the non-zero return code is returned to the caller. The return code is not reset on entry, so a non-zero code from an earlier call also blocks the start. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 2000-GET-NEXT-PROCESS.

outcomes.when_true: PERFORM 2300-UPDATE-PROCESS-STATUS (mark process ACTIVE with start time)
outcomes.when_false: process not started; return code returned to caller

business_rules.name: Check process definition type matches the requested sequence type
business_rules.description: Check process definition type matches the requested sequence type. While building the process sequence, when a process definition's type equals the sequence type requested by the caller, the system adds the process to the in-memory sequence with status READY. Otherwise the definition is skipped. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 1200-BUILD-SEQUENCE.

outcomes.when_true: PERFORM 1210-ADD-TO-SEQUENCE (append with status READY)

business_rules.name: Select the first READY process in sequence order
business_rules.description: Select the first READY process in sequence order. The system scans the sequence table in load order and, at the first process whose status equals READY ('R'), returns that process ID as the next process and stops scanning. Otherwise it continues with the next table entry. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 2100-FIND-NEXT-READY.

outcomes.when_true: LS-NEXT-PROCESS = WS-PROC-ID(ix); EXIT PERFORM

business_rules.name: Route no-ready-process outcome when the sequence is exhausted
business_rules.description: Route no-ready-process outcome when the sequence is exhausted. When the scan passes the last process in the table without finding a READY process, the system clears the next-process ID. The caller paragraph still performs the dependency check with the blank process ID, which then fails the dependency read. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 2100-FIND-NEXT-READY.

outcomes.when_true: MOVE SPACES TO LS-NEXT-PROCESS (no READY process)

business_rules.name: Reject process start at the first failed dependency check
business_rules.sme_review_note: Dependency loop subscript WS-SUB is not declared in PRCSEQ00 or its copybooks (field_id_unresolved).
business_rules.description: Reject process start at the first failed dependency check. While checking the selected process's dependencies one by one, when a check leaves a non-zero return code the system stops checking further dependencies. Otherwise it checks the next dependency. The loop subscript is not declared in the program. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 2200-CHECK-DEPENDENCIES.

outcomes.when_true: EXIT PERFORM - stop checking further dependencies

business_rules.name: Check dependency job is done
business_rules.description: Check dependency job is done. For each dependency of the selected process, when the dependency job's batch-control status is not DONE ('D'), the system applies the hard/soft dependency rule. Otherwise, the system checks the completed job's return code against the dependency's allowed maximum. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 2210-CHECK-DEP-STATUS.

outcomes.when_true: apply hard/soft dependency rule (see BR-015)
outcomes.when_false: check return code against allowed maximum (see BR-016)

business_rules.name: Reject process start while a hard dependency is not done
business_rules.sme_review_note: Dependency table subscript WS-SUB is not declared in scope (field_id_unresolved); capped at medium per partial evidence.
business_rules.description: Reject process start while a hard dependency is not done. When a dependency job is not yet DONE and the dependency type is hard ('H'), the system sets warning return code 4 so the process may not start yet. A soft dependency that is not yet done does not block the process. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 2210-CHECK-DEP-STATUS.

outcomes.when_true: LS-RETURN-CODE = 4 (warning) - process may not start yet

business_rules.name: Enforce dependency return code does not exceed the allowed maximum
business_rules.sme_review_note: Dependency table subscript WS-SUB is not declared in scope (field_id_unresolved); capped at medium per partial evidence.
business_rules.description: Enforce dependency return code does not exceed the allowed maximum. When a dependency job has finished and its return code is greater than the maximum return code allowed for that dependency, the system sets error return code 8 and the process may not start. Otherwise the dependency is satisfied. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 2210-CHECK-DEP-STATUS.

outcomes.when_true: LS-RETURN-CODE = 8 (error) - process may not start

business_rules.name: Check sequence table entry matches the control record job name
business_rules.description: Check sequence table entry matches the control record job name. When refreshing status, the system looks up the sequence table entry whose process ID equals the batch-control job name and copies the control record's status and return code into that entry, then stops the lookup. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 3200-UPDATE-SEQUENCE-TABLE.

outcomes.when_true: WS-PROC-STATUS(ix) = BCT-STATUS; WS-PROC-RC(ix) = BCT-RETURN-CODE; EXIT PERFORM

business_rules.name: Calculate count of active processes per sequence entry
business_rules.description: Calculate count of active processes per sequence entry (per-iteration rule). For each process in the sequence table whose status is ACTIVE ('A'), the system adds 1 to the active-process count; the counter is cleared before the loop. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 3300-CHECK-COMPLETION.

outcomes.when_true: ADD 1 TO WS-ACTIVE-COUNT

business_rules.name: Calculate count of failed processes per sequence entry
business_rules.description: Calculate count of failed processes per sequence entry (per-iteration rule). For each process in the sequence table whose status is ERROR ('E'), the system adds 1 to the error count. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 3300-CHECK-COMPLETION.

outcomes.when_true: ADD 1 TO WS-ERROR-COUNT

business_rules.name: Derive sequence return code 8 when any process failed
business_rules.description: Derive sequence return code 8 when any process failed (accumulated-result rule). After counting process statuses, when the error count is greater than zero the system sets the sequence return code to 8. Otherwise it applies the active-process tier (BR-021). Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 4100-CHECK-FINAL-STATUS.

outcomes.when_true: LS-RETURN-CODE = 8 (error) - at least one process failed

business_rules.name: Derive sequence return code 4 when processes are still active
business_rules.description: Derive sequence return code 4 when processes are still active (accumulated-result rule). When no process has failed and the active-process count is greater than zero, the system sets the sequence return code to 4. Otherwise it sets return code 0. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 4100-CHECK-FINAL-STATUS.

outcomes.when_true: LS-RETURN-CODE = 4 (warning) - processes still active

business_rules.name: Derive process sequence number from load order
business_rules.description: Derive process sequence number from load order (per-iteration rule). For each matching process definition the system adds 1 to the process count, stores the process ID with sequence number equal to that count and sets its status to READY. The accumulated process count bounds every later table scan and the creation of READY control records. No check is made against the 100-entry table limit. Implemented in program PRCSEQ00, paragraph 1210-ADD-TO-SEQUENCE.

condition.text: ADD 1 TO WS-PROCESS-COUNT; MOVE PSR-PROCESS-ID / WS-PROCESS-COUNT / BCT-STAT-READY TO table entry; SET WS-PROC-IX UP BY 1

outcomes.result: process sequence number = load order; initial status READY

business_rules.name: Route batch recovery requests by function code
business_rules.description: Route batch recovery requests by function code. The recovery subprogram selects its path from the caller's function code: 'INIT' opens files, validates the request and sets the recovery mode, 'RECV' performs the recovery, and 'TERM' terminates recovery. Any other code is rejected with 'Invalid function code'. Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 0000-MAIN.

condition.text: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN FUNC-INIT / FUNC-RECV / FUNC-TERM / OTHER

business_rules.name: Route recovery by recovery mode
business_rules.description: Route recovery by recovery mode. The system selects the recovery scope from the recovery mode set at initialisation: 'P' recovers one process, 'S' recovers every control record for the requested process date, and 'A' recovers every control record on file. Any other mode performs no recovery (there is no WHEN OTHER). Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 2000-PROCESS-RECOVERY.

business_rules.name: Require process date on a recovery request
business_rules.description: Require process date on a recovery request. When the recovery request's process date is blank, the system reports 'Process date required' through the error routine (return code 8). Processing then continues. Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 1200-VALIDATE-REQUEST.

outcomes.when_true: error text 'Process date required'; PERFORM 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE (RC 8; processing continues)

business_rules.name: Validate recovery type is a valid recovery type
business_rules.description: Validate recovery type is a valid recovery type. When the requested recovery type is 'P' (process), 'S' (sequence) or 'A' (all), the request is accepted. Otherwise, the system reports 'Invalid recovery type' through the error routine. Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 1200-VALIDATE-REQUEST.

condition.text: EVALUATE LS-RECOVERY-TYPE WHEN 'P' WHEN 'S' WHEN 'A' CONTINUE WHEN OTHER error

business_rules.name: Require process ID for single-process recovery
business_rules.description: Require process ID for single-process recovery. When the recovery mode is process recovery ('P') and no process ID is supplied, the system reports 'Process ID required for process recovery' through the error routine. Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 1300-SET-RECOVERY-MODE.

outcomes.when_true: error text 'Process ID required for process recovery'; PERFORM 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE

business_rules.name: Check process definition is restartable
business_rules.description: Check process definition is restartable. When the failed process's definition is marked restartable (PSR-RESTART = 'Y'), the system chooses the restart action. Otherwise it applies the maximum-restart limit (BR-029). The restart limit is therefore applied only to non-restartable processes. Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 2110-DETERMINE-ACTION.

outcomes.when_true: WS-RECOVERY-ACTION = 'R' (restart)

business_rules.name: Enforce maximum restart count for non-restartable processes
business_rules.description: Enforce maximum restart count for non-restartable processes. When a non-restartable process has been restarted more times than the maximum allowed (BCT-MAX-RESTARTS; value 3 per the upstream narrative), the system chooses the terminate action (status Error, return code 8). Otherwise it chooses the bypass action (status Done, return code 4). Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 2110-DETERMINE-ACTION.

outcomes.when_true: WS-RECOVERY-ACTION = 'T' (terminate: status Error, RC 8)

business_rules.name: Dispatch recovery action restart, bypass or terminate
business_rules.description: Dispatch recovery action restart, bypass or terminate. The system executes the recovery action decided earlier: restart sets the process status to READY, adds 1 to the restart count and records the attempt time; bypass sets status DONE with warning return code 4 and the message 'Process bypassed by recovery'; terminate sets status ERROR with return code 8 and the message 'Process terminated by recovery'. Each action rewrites the batch control record. Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 2120-EXECUTE-RECOVERY.

condition.text: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN WS-ACTION-RESTART / WS-ACTION-BYPASS / WS-ACTION-TERMINATE (no WHEN OTHER)

business_rules.name: Select control records for the requested process date in sequence recovery
business_rules.description: Select control records for the requested process date in sequence recovery. While browsing the batch control file, when a control record's process date equals the requested process date, the system recovers that process. Otherwise the record is skipped. Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 2200-RECOVER-SEQUENCE.

outcomes.when_true: LS-PROCESS-ID = BCT-JOB-NAME; PERFORM 2100-RECOVER-PROCESS

business_rules.name: Select recovery completion message by return code
business_rules.description: Select recovery completion message by return code. When recovery ends with return code zero, the system reports 'Recovery completed successfully'. Otherwise it reports 'Recovery completed with errors'. The message is passed to the shared error-processing program ERRPROC. Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 3100-UPDATE-FINAL-STATUS.

outcomes.when_true: message 'Recovery completed successfully'

business_rules.name: Calculate persisted restart count on each restart
business_rules.description: Calculate persisted restart count on each restart. Each time recovery restarts a process, the system sets its status to READY, adds 1 to the restart count stored in the batch control record and records the attempt timestamp. The accumulated count is compared with the maximum restarts on later recoveries (BR-029). Implemented in program RCVPRC00, paragraph 2121-RESTART-PROCESS.

condition.text: ADD 1 TO BCT-RESTART-COUNT (with BCT-STATUS = BCT-STAT-READY and attempt timestamp)

outcomes.result: restart count incremented by 1 and persisted

business_rules.name: Calculate position percentage change against previous value
business_rules.sme_review_note: Operands POS-CURRENT-VALUE and POS-PREVIOUS-VALUE are not declared in POSREC or any layout in scope (field_id_unresolved), so their source and type are unknown; result field WS-POS-CHANGE-PCT has no Field ID; a zero previous value is not guarded (no ON SIZE ERROR). Transaction activity and summary totals come from 2210/2220/2310/2320/2330 - paragraphs not present in the source.
business_rules.description: Calculate position percentage change against previous value (per-iteration rule). For each position record on the report the system computes change % = (current value - previous value) / previous value x 100 and writes it on the detail line. A previous value of zero is not guarded. The two value fields are not declared in the program's layouts. Implemented in program RPTPOS00, paragraph 2110-FORMAT-POSITION.

outcomes.result: percentage change per position written on the detail line

business_rules.name: Calculate return code counts by severity per program
business_rules.description: Calculate return code counts by severity per program. For the return-code analysis report the system reads the logged return codes grouped by program ID and, for each program, derives the total number of logged codes and the number with status S (success), W (warning), E (error) and F (severe), ordered by program ID. Implemented in program RTNANA00, paragraph P200-PROCESS-ANALYSIS.

outcomes.result: one summary row per program ID with total, success, warning, error and severe counts

business_rules.name: Calculate grand totals of return code counts per fetched program row
business_rules.sme_review_note: FETCH statement SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0051-STMT-000026 is flagged ambiguous upstream (statement_ambiguous): it fetches into numeric-edited fields (PIC ZZZ,ZZ9) that are then used as ADD operands; behaviour is compiler-dependent.
business_rules.description: Calculate grand totals of return code counts per fetched program row (per-iteration rule). For each program row fetched successfully, the system adds the row's total, success, warning, error and severe counts to the matching grand totals. Rows not fetched successfully are skipped. Implemented in program RTNANA00, paragraph P220-PROCESS-DETAIL.

condition.text: ADD WS-DTL-TOTAL TO WS-PROGRAM-COUNT; ADD WS-DTL-SUCCESS TO WS-SUCCESS-COUNT; ADD WS-DTL-WARNING TO WS-WARNING-COUNT; ADD WS-DTL-ERROR TO WS-ERROR-COUNT; ADD WS-DTL-SEVERE TO WS-SEVERE-COUNT

outcomes.result: grand totals += row counts for each successfully fetched row

business_rules.name: Derive return code analysis report totals line
business_rules.description: Derive return code analysis report totals line (accumulated-result rule). After all program rows have been processed, the system writes a TOTALS line carrying the grand totals of logged codes and of success, warning, error and severe codes over all programs. Implemented in program RTNANA00, paragraph P300-GENERATE-REPORT.

condition.text: MOVE 'TOTALS' TO WS-DTL-PROGRAM; MOVE WS-PROGRAM-COUNT / WS-SUCCESS-COUNT / WS-WARNING-COUNT / WS-ERROR-COUNT / WS-SEVERE-COUNT TO detail fields; WRITE

outcomes.result: TOTALS line written after the detail lines

business_rules.name: Route return code service requests by request type
business_rules.description: Route return code service requests by request type. The return-code service selects its action from the request type: 'I' initialises (resets codes, status SUCCESS, response 0), 'S' sets a new return code, 'G' returns the current and highest codes and status, 'L' logs the code to the RTNCODES table, and 'A' analyses logged codes over a time window. Any other request type performs nothing and leaves the response code unchanged. Implemented in program RTNCDE00, unnamed first paragraph.

condition.text: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN RC-INITIALIZE / RC-SET-CODE / RC-GET-CODE / RC-LOG-CODE / RC-ANALYZE (no WHEN OTHER)

business_rules.name: Derive highest return code across calls
business_rules.description: Derive highest return code across calls. When a new return code is set and it is greater than the highest code recorded so far, the system records it as the new highest code. Otherwise the highest code is kept. In both cases the current code becomes the new code. The high-water mark is kept in the caller's area. Implemented in program RTNCDE00, paragraph P200-SET-RETURN-CODE.

outcomes.when_true: RC-HIGHEST-CODE = RC-NEW-CODE

business_rules.name: Derive return code severity status from code range
business_rules.description: Derive return code severity status from code range. When a new return code is set, the system classifies it: 0 is SUCCESS ('S'), 1 to 4 is WARNING ('W'), 5 to 8 is ERROR ('E'), and any other value is SEVERE ('F'). Implemented in program RTNCDE00, paragraph P200-SET-RETURN-CODE.

condition.text: EVALUATE RC-NEW-CODE WHEN 0 / WHEN 1 THRU 4 / WHEN 5 THRU 8 / WHEN OTHER

business_rules.name: Calculate return code count, maximum and minimum for a program within a time window
business_rules.description: Calculate return code count, maximum and minimum for a program within a time window. On an analyse request the system counts the logged return codes of one program between the caller's start and end timestamps and derives the highest and lowest logged code. Implemented in program RTNCDE00, paragraph P500-ANALYZE-CODES.

condition.text: SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(RETURN_CODE), MIN(RETURN_CODE) FROM RTNCODES WHERE PROGRAM_ID = :program AND TIMESTAMP BETWEEN :start AND :end

outcomes.result: count, highest and lowest logged return code for the program within the time window

business_rules.name: Route DB2 commit control requests by function code
business_rules.description: Route DB2 commit control requests by function code. The commit controller selects its action from the caller's function code: 'INIT' clears the commit statistics, 'CMIT' commits, 'RBAK' rolls back, 'SAVE' creates a savepoint, 'REST' rolls back to the savepoint and 'STAT' displays the counters. Any other code is rejected with return code 12 and reported through ERRPROC. Implemented in program DB2CMT, paragraph 0000-MAIN.

condition.text: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN FUNC-INIT / FUNC-CMIT / FUNC-RBACK / FUNC-SAVE / FUNC-REST / FUNC-STAT / OTHER

business_rules.name: Enforce commit when records processed reach the commit frequency or commit is forced
business_rules.description: Enforce commit when records processed reach the commit frequency or commit is forced. When the caller's count of records processed is greater than or equal to the caller-supplied commit frequency, or the caller sets the force-commit indicator ('Y'), the system issues a DB2 COMMIT. Otherwise no commit is issued and this call does not set the return code. Implemented in program DB2CMT, paragraph 2000-COMMIT.

outcomes.when_true: PERFORM 2100-ISSUE-COMMIT (EXEC SQL COMMIT WORK)
